correctness.rationale: Equality with the inverse forces common domain S and a square-identity automorphism of F_n[S]. Its connected components are precisely consecutive selected runs. Alternating path automorphisms are trivial except for odd lengths at least three (C2), and component isomorphism types depend only on length and endpoint height as stated. Involutions in the resulting wreath products pair j components in m!/(2^j j!(m-2j)!) ways, with g^j coherent isomorphisms, while each fixed component contributes the identity and possibly reversal. Multiplying factors and summing domains proves the entire bivariate formula for every n; rank-two and rank-(n-1) formulas follow by explicit domain analysis. The independently coded brute-force test enumerated all partial involutions n<=8 and matched every (f,t) coefficient, with further exact formula checks through n=12. Finite tests corroborate but do not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The self-inverse elements form a canonical, structurally meaningful subset of the finite-fence inverse monoid. The result supplies every rank and both involution cycle parameters for every size, not an arbitrary finite slice. The striking parity dependence of rank n-1, plus simple rank-two coefficient and asymmetric full-rank behavior, reveal natural differences between alternating-poset symmetries. The formula is self-contained and computable from run inventories, enabling subsequent questions about growth and randomly selected involutive partial automorphisms. Complexity and lack of an elementary all-n total are expressly acknowledged.
